gloss: to throb; to flutter; to be excited

definitions.gloss: to throb; to flutter; to be excited
definitions.explanation: For one's heart to beat fast with excitement, anticipation, or romantic feelings. Describes a positive emotional flutter.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}を{見|み}ると{胸|むね}がときめく。
examples.english: My heart flutters when I see him.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{出会|であ}いにときめいている。
examples.english: I'm excited about meeting someone new.

examples.japanese: ときめきを{感|かん}じなくなった。
examples.english: I stopped feeling that flutter of excitement.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}). No pair verb.

KANJI:
Sometimes written as {時|とき}めく, though hiragana is standard.

USAGE:
ときめく describes a positive emotional excitement, often associated with romance, new experiences, or anticipation. It's a softer, more pleasant sensation than anxiety.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{胸|むね}がときめく (heart flutters)
・ときめきを{感|かん}じる (to feel excitement)
・ときめく{出会|であ}い (exciting encounter)

RELATED NOUN:
ときめき - flutter, excitement, thrill
・ときめきがある (to feel excitement)
・ときめきを{与|あた}える (to give someone a thrill)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Famously used in Marie Kondo's tidying philosophy: 「ときめくかどうか」(whether it sparks joy) as a criterion for keeping possessions.

SIMILAR WORDS:
・どきどきする - heart pounding (can be anxiety or excitement)
・わくわくする - to be excited (anticipation-focused)
・{興奮|こうふん}する - to be excited (stronger, more general)
